full_judgment:
2. The petitioners case, in short, is that one Md Baja Mondal, the predecessor of the petitioners, took lease of the case land from ex-landlord. Opposite-Party No. 2 while the suit land was in his khas possession. On 12th Jaishta, 1354 BS Md Haja Mondal executed and registered a kabuliyat in favour of the Landlord. During Revisional Settlement Operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the ex-landlord, opposite-party No. 2. The title of the petitioners predecessor having been clouded on account of the said wrong record, he instituted the aforesaid suit against the Opposite-Parties for declaration of his title in the suit land. 

 3. Opposite-party No. 1 filed written statement contending, inter alia that the suit land did not belong exclusively to ex-landlord opposite-party No. 2, Srijukta Babu Bimalendu Bhusan Roy and, as such, petitioners' predecessor, Md Haja Mondal did not acquire title to the entire suit land: That co-sharers of opposite-party No. 2 had left Bangladesh and acquired citizenship of India and, as such, their properties had been declared as khas land, being vested to the Government. That the suit land along with 2.48 acres of land of other plots became khas property of Government by virtue of the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act: That, in the above circumstances, the suit was liable to be dismissed with costs.
